newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech shares steady, but mkt nervous ahead of vote.
newsitem.headline: Czech shares steady, but mkt nervous ahead of vote.

text.p: Czech shares showed little change in moderate trading on Friday, but analysts said the calm on the surface belied a market nervous of next week's confidence vote in the government.
Komercni Banka was one of the few blue chips to make a significant move, falling 43 crowns to 1,945, but it still was not enough to budge the PX50 index, which closed unchanged at 497.6.
Dealers said investors were taking a wait and see attitude ahead of the vote which Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus is expected to survive, though barely.
There's no interest right now among investors because of the uncertainty in the Czech crown and the government's confidence vote," Petr Opocensky of Citicorp Securities in Prague told Reuters.
"This feeling will last at least until the confidence vote, ansd maybe longer," he said.
Confectioner Cokoladovny, majority owned by a consortium of Swiss Nestle SA and France's Danone, continued its upward path, rising 145 crowns to 4,050.

Dealers said the issue has gained favour with investors in recent days after the firm announced it would propose paying a 70 crown gross dividend per share on 1996 earnings, after 50 crowns in the previous year.
Cokoladovny posted net profit of 735 million crowns in 1996, after 516 million in 1995.
The firm holds its annual general meeting on June 31, dividends will be paid to shareholders registered on June 23.
The Swiss-French consortium Cokoladovny Partners hold an 81 percent stake in the Czech company.
